inputs.goal: redesign a hospital discharge form so patients actually read it
inputs.msg: My discharge form is complete but nobody reads it. I'm told to make it 'clearer', but I think it's written for the hospital's liability, not the patient's understanding.

inputs.goal: make a protest poster that still has bite
inputs.msg: My protest poster keeps getting called 'striking' and 'beautiful', and that praise makes me feel like it's failed — it's become decorative, something to admire instead of act on.

inputs.goal: design a tutorial that respects the player
inputs.msg: My game tutorial holds the player's hand through everything. It works — nobody gets stuck — but nobody discovers anything, and the game feels solved before it starts.

inputs.goal: design a memorial people actually stop at
inputs.msg: I designed a memorial and watched people walk straight past it. It's dignified and tasteful, and I think that's exactly the problem — it's so respectful it's invisible.

inputs.goal: design a consent flow that is honest
inputs.msg: My cookie consent flow is technically compliant, but I built it so people click 'accept all', and I know that's the point, and I feel like a fraud.

inputs.goal: edit a documentary fairly
inputs.msg: In the edit, my subject keeps coming across as guilty. I'm not adding anything false — just the order of the cuts — but the truth of the footage and the feeling of the sequence are pulling apart.

inputs.goal: design honest sustainability labelling
inputs.msg: The fabric is recycled, that part's real, but the big 'sustainable' label makes a whole-garment claim the garment can't back, and I'm the one designing the tag.

inputs.goal: design a smart speaker that does not feel like surveillance
inputs.msg: Our smart speaker's always-on mic is genuinely useful, but in a home it feels like surveillance, and the little 'listening' light somehow makes it worse, not better.

inputs.goal: design a dashboard that surfaces what matters
inputs.msg: My dashboard shows everything and the user sees nothing — I keep adding charts to look thorough, but it just buries the one number that actually matters.

inputs.goal: make a rebrand that is actually distinct
inputs.msg: The rebrand brief says 'clean and modern', and that's killing me — every competitor says the same, and I can't tell if mine is actually different or just another sans-serif on white.

inputs.goal: design an onboarding that does not overwhelm
inputs.msg: My fintech onboarding has twelve steps 'to be safe', and users drop off halfway — but every step is there because a stakeholder was scared of something.

inputs.goal: make a data visualisation that is honest
inputs.msg: My chart is technically accurate, but the axis I chose makes a tiny change look enormous, and that dramatic version is exactly the story the team wants to tell.

inputs.goal: design a clinic queue that feels fair
inputs.msg: My clinic token system is efficient, but people feel cheated when someone walks in and is seen first for a 'quick' thing, and the efficiency is somehow making the unfairness louder.

inputs.goal: design a notification that respects attention
inputs.msg: My streak notifications boost retention, they really work — but I've built something that punishes people for having a life outside the app.

inputs.goal: make a form that does not misgender people
inputs.msg: There's a required gender dropdown with two options because the database wants it that way, and I'm the one who has to design the thing that erases people.

inputs.goal: design a feed that does not trap people
inputs.msg: The recommendation feed works — engagement is up — but I've built something that keeps people scrolling long past the point they actually wanted to stop.

inputs.goal: design packaging that is not wasteful theatre
inputs.msg: The unboxing needs layers and tissue to feel premium, and it does feel premium — for about thirty seconds, and then it's all landfill.

inputs.goal: write an error message that does not blame the user
inputs.msg: My error copy just says 'invalid input', and I keep writing it that way, as if it's the user's fault that the system decided to be strict.

inputs.goal: design a museum route that does not exhaust people
inputs.msg: The layout forces everyone through every gallery for 'completeness', and by room eight nobody is looking at anything — they're just walking to the exit.

inputs.goal: make a pricing page that is not manipulative
inputs.msg: The 'most popular' badge and the struck-through price work — conversions are up — but I designed them to steer people, not to inform them, and I know the difference.

inputs.goal: design a returns process that is not hostile
inputs.msg: My returns flow is deliberately annoying to cut return rates, and it works — but I'm the one adding friction to punish honest customers for a policy decision.

inputs.goal: choose type that people can actually read
inputs.msg: My low-contrast grey type looks elegant and the client loves it, but I know people with low vision can't read it, and I keep choosing the elegant version anyway.

inputs.goal: design an assistant that does not fake empathy
inputs.msg: My chatbot says 'I understand how you feel' when it understands nothing, and users thank it warmly, and that gratitude is the part that unsettles me.

inputs.goal: design station signage for a multilingual city
inputs.msg: My wayfinding assumes everyone reads English, in a city where half the people at the station don't, and 'clean' design is my excuse for not adding the other scripts.

inputs.goal: design a quiz app that rewards thinking not speed
inputs.msg: My quiz app scores on speed, so students learn to answer fast instead of think, and the leaderboard is the thing they're actually playing, not the subject.

inputs.goal: photograph a community without reducing them
inputs.msg: I shot the campaign for the NGO, and the images that raise the most money are the ones that show the community as most helpless, and those are the ones getting picked.

inputs.goal: design a trial that does not rely on forgetting
inputs.msg: The free trial needs a card and auto-renews, and it converts because people forget to cancel, and I keep realising that forgetting IS the business model.

inputs.goal: design a shelf logo I am not embarrassed by
inputs.msg: The logo has to shout to compete on a crowded shelf, and I've made something loud and aggressive that does the job and that I can't actually stand to look at.

inputs.goal: design a game economy that is not built on frustration
inputs.msg: My mobile game's timers manufacture the urge to pay to skip the wait, and the 'fun' is really just friction I engineered so I can sell people relief from it.

inputs.goal: design a grievance form people can finish
inputs.msg: The civic complaint form is so long that most people give up, and then the low number of complaints gets reported upward as 'high satisfaction'.
